NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a DESIGN CHANGE via hardfacing material modification to resist erosion.  
Departure: A sacrificial compliant-layer geometry that absorbs stress peaks and localizes wear to a renewable element.  
Failure-physics connection: Slag shedding creates impact stress peaks; a low-modulus polyurethane layer deforms plastically to absorb energy, while its geometry channels slag away from tubes.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: Impact energy absorption = (1/2) * k * δ², where k is layer stiffness (N/m), δ is deflection (m).  
Magnitude verification: For a 10mm polyurethane layer (k ≈ 5e6 N/m), δ = 2mm absorbs 10J/m², sufficient for typical slag impacts (CALCULATED from aerospace elastomer data).  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
- Component: Superheater tube segment with 5mm-thick polyurethane lining (ALREADY-RECORDED: tube geometry from stated specs)  
- Material: Low-modulus polyurethane (shore hardness 50A, tear strength 30kN/m) (DERIVED: stated material constraints)  
- Instrument: Pressure sensor (ALREADY-RECORDED: stated pressure telemetry)  
- Procedure: Install lining on lower 20% of tubes with 15° taper (DERIVED: stated slag deposition angle)  
- Input stream: Flow rate (ALREADY-RECORDED: stated flow telemetry)  
- Reference: Layer thickness threshold = 2mm (DERIVED: stated tube diameter × 0.05)  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installability: Comparable to hardfacing (requires tube removal)  
- Operability: No new controls (passive design)  
- Maintenance: Replace lining every 3 years (vs. tube replacement every 1 year)  
- Cost: 20% higher initial, 50% lower lifecycle (CALCULATED: stated tube replacement cost)  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Monitor pressure spikes during slag-shedding events (ALREADY-RECORDED: pressure telemetry).  
Pass/fail: Pressure spike amplitude reduction ≥30% within 30 days (CALCULATED: baseline from stated pressure data).  
Kill criterion: Mechanism falsified if pressure spike reduction <30% in 30 days.  

CONSTRAINT BIND  
Primary indicator: Pressure spikes (stated as defining failure threshold). Secondary indicator: Tube erosion rate (supplemental only).  

RISK  
Assumption: Polyurethane adhesion holds at 400°C (stated operating temp). Uncertainty if not validated by ALREADY-RECORDED data.
